notes: I1: PCI is identified as volumetric in the Experimental Section (main, p. 2, journal p. 9508): 'a volumetric measurement using a pressure composition isotherm (PCI) manufactured by the Advanced Materials Corporation of Pittsburgh, PA'. 'PIC' in the Section 4 quote is the paper's typo for PCI. Figure 11B (main, p. 6) plots H2 uptake (%) against pressure (atm, 0-70) for Ni20(arc) 'at liquid nitrogen temperature'. A gravimetric (IGA) value is also reported: 0.4 wt % at -200 C and 6 atm (main, p. 6). The high-temperature values (2.3 and 2.8 wt %) are from quantitative TPD after charging at 35 or 50 atm and are not relied on for I1. I2: Ni20(arc) is defined (main, p. 2) as the wall deposit from arc discharge of the Ni(20 wt %) and graphite(80 wt %) mixture, i.e. Ni20C80(arc); with 16.5 wt % Ni by TPO, carbon is the majority component by mass, so it is a metal-decorated carbon composite under protocol section 3. The PCI isotherm (Figure 11B) is on this sample. I4: the BET area (130 m2/g, and 284 m2/g after cycling) is for Ni20(arc), the sample with the 77 K PCI isotherm; BET by Nova 3000 at liquid-nitrogen temperature (Experimental Section). I5: the first sentence is 44 words, so it is truncated with an ellipsis to respect the 40-word limit. No retraction notice, not a review, and no statement that the uptake values were published before.
